instructions: You are Gemini (Veo). Follow the Drive doc 'Titan Reliquary/VIDEO_START_HERE (for Gemini Veo)'. Use your best Veo model WITH native audio. Make EVERY take listed (3 takes per shot: same prompt, different seeds). Save each clip to Titan Reliquary/art-incoming-video (Gemini Veo clips)/artreq_20261001-1930_splash-film-v2/ with the exact file_name. When done, create artreq_20261001-1930_splash-film-v2.DONE.txt in Titan Reliquary/art-requests-video (Gemini Veo)/ listing every file as 'file_name | ok' or 'file_name | skipped: reason', plus your model name and the date. If you cannot make video, write artreq_20261001-1930_splash-film-v2.FAILED.txt saying so.
purpose: The opening film of a private coin-collection app, shown once each time the app opens on a phone (portrait) or desktop (landscape). It must feel like the opening of a luxury-watch or private-bank commercial. The app fades in over the final dark frame, so the LAST 1.5 SECONDS MUST GO TO NEAR-BLACK (no cut, a smooth fade of the light).

deliverable_spec.container: MP4 (H.264 or H.265). If your tool also offers a ProRes or a higher-quality file, save that too with the same name plus _hq.
deliverable_spec.resolution: 9:16 = 1080x1920 or higher; 16:9 = 1920x1080 or higher. Never upscale low-res output as a substitute.
deliverable_spec.duration: exactly 8 seconds (if your tool's max is shorter, make the longest it allows and say so in the DONE file)
deliverable_spec.audio: If your model generates audio (Veo 3 does): include a restrained, high-end sound design track. Silence, then a soft electrical click of the light, then deep mechanical bolt thunks, a low door groan, an airy room tone opening up, and a single soft metallic ring at the coin. No music, no voice, no whooshes. ALSO save a silent version of the same take with the suffix _silent if your tool can.
deliverable_spec.safe_area: keep the key action inside the central 80% (phones crop edges); keep the top 12% and bottom 18% free of important detail (app buttons and captions sit there)
deliverable_spec.end_frame: from second 6.5 to 8.0 the light fades smoothly to near-black (RGB below 12); the final frame must be almost black and still
deliverable_spec.continuity: ONE continuous shot per clip: no cuts, no dissolves, no jump in camera position

global_style: Photoreal live-action cinematography, as if shot on an ARRI Alexa 65 with Panavision anamorphic primes on a motion-control rig. 24 fps, 180-degree shutter (natural motion blur), shallow depth of field, gentle anamorphic oval bokeh, very subtle horizontal flare only from the brightest highlight. Lighting: one hard warm tungsten key (3200 K) plus a faint cool fill (5600 K, very low); deep, rich, clean blacks; no haze except where the shot says dust. Materials must read as REAL: brushed and bead-blasted steel with micro-scratches, mirror-polished chrome bolts that reflect the light, true silver with soft toning, black velvet that absorbs light. Grade: neutral-warm, filmic highlight roll-off, subtle 35 mm grain. Camera moves are slow, smooth and weighted (motion control), never handheld.
negative: no text, no titles, no numbers, no logos, no brand names, no watermark, no UI; no people, hands, faces or silhouettes; no cartoon, no anime, no illustration, no video-game or CGI-render look, no plastic or rubbery metal; no glowing sci-fi lines, no neon, no blue holograms, no particles that look like sparkles or fairy dust, no lens-flare spam, no camera shake, no speed ramps, no fast zooms; no morphing, melting or wobbling objects; the door, bolts and coin must stay rigid and keep their shape; no extra doors or duplicated coins; no invented legible inscriptions on any coin
coin_rule: The coin is a generic silver crown-size coin (about 38 mm) with a classical portrait relief on one side and a heraldic eagle on the other. Any lettering must be too small or soft to read. Never show a recognisable real coin design and never invent readable text.

shots.A: SHOT A, 'The Vault Door' (8.0 s, one continuous shot). 0.0-0.8 s: pure black, silence. 0.8-1.6 s: a single warm tungsten spotlight clicks on from the upper left and rakes across the face of a colossal circular bank-vault door (3 m diameter, brushed blackened steel, a ring of 12 mirror-polished chrome locking bolts around the edge, a polished chrome five-spoke handwheel in the centre over a fine engraved guilloché pattern). The camera is locked off, centred on the door, slightly low, with a 50 mm anamorphic. 1.6-3.0 s: the handwheel turns a quarter turn with weight; the 12 bolts retract in sequence, clockwise from the top, each one sliding back with a precise mechanical stop. 3.0-4.8 s: the door swings slowly open toward camera-left on three massive hinge barrels; a blade of warm light and fine floating dust spills through the widening gap and across a polished black stone floor, which reflects it. 4.8-6.5 s: the camera dollies forward smoothly through the opening into a small dark chamber, where a single silver coin rests flat on a square of black velvet on a black pedestal under one tight top-down spotlight; focus racks from the door edge to the coin; the coin's rim catches a bright specular highlight. 6.5-8.0 s: the camera settles; the spotlight slowly dims to near-black, leaving the faint coin rim glinting last.
shots.B: SHOT B, 'The Coin' (8.0 s, one continuous shot, extreme macro, 100 mm macro lens). 0.0-0.7 s: black. 0.7-2.5 s: a thin, sharp line of warm light (like a light-painting strip) sweeps slowly left to right across the frosted classical-portrait relief of a silver crown coin lying on a black mirror surface, revealing the contrast between frosted devices and mirror field, like a luxury-watch dial commercial. 2.5-5.5 s: the coin rotates slowly on its own axis (about 120 degrees) on the black mirror, which shows a perfect soft reflection; a few individual dust motes drift slowly through the light beam; the focus racks from the finely reeded edge to the portrait. 5.5-6.5 s: the camera pulls back slightly to show the whole coin, rim-lit with a thin bright halo on a pure black background. 6.5-8.0 s: the light fades to near-black, the last rim highlight disappearing last.
shots.C: SHOT C, 'Struck' (8.0 s, one continuous shot, macro, slow motion feel). 0.0-0.6 s: black. 0.6-3.0 s: in a dark foundry a thin stream of molten silver, glowing bright orange-white, pours from a graphite crucible into a steel mould; a few real sparks arc away; heat shimmer. 3.0-5.5 s: the camera tracks slowly sideways along a polished steel workbench past freshly cast silver bars cooling from dull to gleaming, to a heavy antique screw coining press. 5.5-6.5 s: the press descends once; a burst of reflected light flashes off a freshly struck bright silver coin sitting in the collar of the die. 6.5-8.0 s: everything fades to near-black except the last glint on the new coin. Warm light only; restrained and elegant, not an action movie.
